_note: SessionStart: injects a tiny luamemo digest (memo brief) into the session's context so the agent knows what persistent memory + codebase map exist without being asked. The script (hooks/claude/session_start.sh) wraps it as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (plain stdout is NOT reliably injected); memo reads the settings itself (the project's .luamemorc, found from the project directory up, over ~/.luamemorc) — the hook only starts it there. LUAMEMO_ANY_PROJECT=1: the plugin is luamemo's own, so a project without a .luamemorc of its own still gets the brief (memo finds a global ~/.luamemorc); the script run by `memo agent install` does not set it. memo is run through bash: a git checkout of the plugin may not keep its executable bit. memo brief is hard-capped by timeout and fail-soft, so the hook never blocks or errors the session.
_note2: UserPromptSubmit: what the user says (a correction, a standing rule) reaches memory without the agent having to remember to call memory_sense — the script sends the prompt to `memo sense` in the background and prints nothing. PreToolUse: in a project that has a .luamemorc, a write under ~/.claude/projects/*/memory/ is denied with a pointer to the luamemo tools (Claude Code's file memory is invisible to luamemo); other projects are untouched. All three run through bash (an exec bit may not survive a checkout) and never block or fail the session.
